correctness.rationale: For every nonzero integer \(a\) and integer initial values with all positive-index terms nonzero, \(x_n=(Cn+D)a^{n-1}\). Exact cancellation yields the central rational quotient. If \(CD\ne0\), reduce \(Cj+D\) to coprime \(Aj+B\). Dirichlet gives infinitely many primes \(p\equiv B\pmod A\) not dividing a; \(j=k=(p-B)/A\) gives exactly one p in the denominator and none in the numerator interval, proving \(\nu_p=-1\). Conversely both \(C=0\) and \(D=0\) yield explicit integer coefficients and index divisibility. The same p witnesses rule out divisibility in excluded cases. Exact arithmetic verified 800 finite parameter cases but is only supplemental.

originality.rationale: Primary 2023 source explicitly leaves the binomid-versus-divisible order-two question open and gives only zero-initial sufficiency. A 2022 broad study classifies sequences already known divisible and does not imply the converse. Indexed searches for exact formulas, affine reductions and related formulations revealed no domination; earlier companion Lucas and p-adic quotient work have distinct scope and claims. The new infinite central-prime obstruction is not contained in the checked published statements; residual unindexed equivalence is possible.
residual_risks: An equivalent affine-sequence binomid criterion could appear in classical Fontené–Ward or arithmetic-progression binomial literature without the searched terminology.
No exhaustive global novelty guarantee follows from the queried databases.

value.rationale: This is a complete classification of the natural repeated-characteristic-root branch of a published open classification problem. It proves a sharp binomid↔divisibility boundary, including every nonzero-initial exception, and an infinite family of distinct denominator-prime obstructions. The family is structurally determined by characteristic discriminant zero, not arbitrarily sliced parameters; it supplies a usable result on the integrality of generalized binomial coefficients.
